subject: Dedicated GPU pool: sizing, throughput & pricing proposal
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cyclone.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@cyclone.ai>
Date: 2026-11-24T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated GPU pool: perf targets and rough pricing ask

Marcus —

Thanks for the demo last week. We liked the latency behavior but need a Dedicated (reserved) path for predictable production traffic. Two requests to start the conversation:

1) Can you provide a sizing recommendation for a Dedicated GPU pool to support our baseline workload (approx 350 concurrent interactive users, average 1.2 requests/minute per user, 400 tokens avg prompt + 600 tokens avg response)? We care about maintaining p95 < 250ms and p99 < 450ms for single-turn chat flows.

2) High level committed pricing (monthly) and discount tiers for 6/12/24 month reserved commits (we are evaluating vendor TCO). If you have benchmark artifacts or traces that justify the sizing/pricing, please share.

We can share a sample request trace if that helps.

—Elena
Elena Torres
VP Engineering, Cyclone AI
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cyclone.ai>
Cc: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@cyclone.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T12:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU pool: perf targets and rough pricing ask

Elena —

Thanks — attaching a concise benchmark pack and an initial sizing sketch (attached: redwood-dedicated-benchmark-20261124.csv, p99-traces-8k-window.png). Quick summary up front:

- Based on your numbers, our emulated load suggests a ~450 rps steady-state throughput at 8k context with a 3-node pool of A100-equivalent workers (continuous batching enabled, prefix caching turned on for repeated user system prompts). That equates to ~1.2–1.6M generated tokens/minute.
- Observed latencies (8k window, 1 GPU worker tasks): p50 ~95ms, p95 ~180ms, p99 ~340–380ms. So hitting your p95 target is comfortable; p99 is close to your limit and benefits from an extra worker and cache hits.
- Recommended committed configuration to meet p99 <450ms with headroom: 3x workers with autoscale to 5x on burst. For steady production we recommend a 12-month commit sized to 3 workers; we can add burst credits for traffic spikes.

Preliminary pricing (ballpark):
- 6-month commit (3-worker baseline): list price $52K/mo, estimated commercial discount ~10% off list
- 12-month commit (3-worker baseline): list price $52K/mo, typical discount ~18% off list + 5% volume rebate if central spend crosses $600K/year
- 24-month commit: further structuring possible (additional 3–5% uplift on discounts)

I'll loop our cost lead and infra engineer to confirm exact GPU-hour math and to produce a mutual action plan (MAP). Do you want us to mock-import a 48h trace to run a Cyclone-shaped load test?

Thanks,
Marcus
Account Exec — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T13:10:00-08:00
Subject: Internal: Cyclone (DEAL-8812) — ask for sizing validation + discount guidance

Team — forwarding Cyclone's ask and our quick reply. Key points: they want p95 <250ms, p99 <450ms; estimated steady baseline equates to ~450 rps at 8k window with 3-worker pool.

Can engineering validate: (a) 3-worker baseline with autoscale to 5 is technically sufficient for p99 headroom given their token mix, and (b) confirm GPU-hours and expected amortized cost so I can firm up the pricing.

Finance/RevOps (Neha) — can you confirm whether 18% off list for 12-month + 5% volume rebate (if annual > $600K) is within guardrails? If not, what's the authorized discount band for this ARR band?

We should also attach the CSV and p99 traces to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks — Marcus
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T15:02:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Cyclone (DEAL-8812) — ask for sizing validation + discount guidance

Marcus —

18% for 12 months + 5% rebate is reasonable for a mid-market ARR profile if we get a formal commit (SOW + monthly minimum). Approve moving forward to engineering validation. Ask RevOps to prepare a pricing sheet with list vs net diff and a clause for committed burst credits (so we preserve margin on sudden spikes).

Vanessa
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-30T10:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Internal: Cyclone (DEAL-8812) — engineering sizing notes

Quick engineering readout after a targeted replay of their sample traces:

- Setup used: 3xA100-equivalent workers, continuous batching, prefix/KV cache configured for session prompts.
- Observed steady throughput: 420–480 rps (variance depends on user concurrency patterns).
- Latency: p95 165–200ms (consistent), p99 320–390ms. Under synthetic heavy tails (30% longer responses) p99 crossed 450ms occasionally.
- Recommendation: 12-month commit for 3 workers, include autoscale headroom to 5 (burst credits or pre-allocated spare capacity). If Cyclone cannot accept autoscale, bump baseline to 4 workers to ensure p99 margin (cost delta ~+33% baseline).
- Estimated GPU-hours: ~22,000 GPU-hours/month for 3 workers baseline (24/7 serving assumptions + generation load).

I attached the raw CSV export and p99 trace images to the HubSpot deal.

—Karthik
Senior Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@cyclone.ai>
Cc: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@cyclone.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-05T17:03:00-08:00
Subject: Dedicated commit proposal and next steps (DEAL-8812)

Elena —

Appreciate the patience. Based on our validated runs and internal pricing guardrails, please find an actionable proposal:

1) Recommended commitment: 12-month Dedicated baseline sized to 3 workers (A100-equivalent) with autoscale to 5 workers for bursts. This meets your p95 <250ms target and generally keeps p99 under 450ms with cache behavior; Karthik noted occasional p99 cases under heavy tails, which autoscale will mitigate.

2) Pricing (monthly, net after discounts):
   - List baseline: $52,000/mo
   - 12-month net: $42,640/mo (18% off list)
   - Volume rebate: additional 5% applied at renewal if spend > $600K/12 months
   - Optional baseline bump to 4 workers (no autoscale) to guarantee p99 headroom: $56,000/mo net (12-month structured discount)

3) Commercial notes and packaging:
   - Commit includes defined monthly minimum (to avoid churned burst billing) and 1000 burst credits/mo for autoscale events; additional burst use invoiced at reserved unit rates.
   - SLA: 99.9% uptime for Dedicated; latency SLOs are not contractually guaranteed but we will include operational runbooks and a two-week acceptance window to validate p99 targets.

4) Next actions (MAP):
   - Cyclone: confirm preferred commit term (6/12/24) and whether autoscale is acceptable.
   - Redwood: RevOps will send formal pricing sheet + draft SOW; Eng will standby to run a 48–72h shaped load with Cyclone sample traces to sign off latency expectations.

Attachments: commit-pricing-proposal-v1.pdf, redwood-dedicated-benchmark-20261124.csv, p99-traces-8k-window.png

If that looks good I can circulate the formal doc and propose a contract call next week.

Cheers,
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
